name: Lane WIP counts — n/limit, loud when over
description: Epics-mode column headers show 'n/limit' for lanes with a configured wip_limit (n = total epics in lane, board-wide like the protocol's check — not the filtered count). Over-limit renders in a loud red state with a title explaining. Advise-only: no drop is ever refused because of a limit.
acceptance_criteria: A lane with a wip_limit renders its epics-mode header count as 'n/limit'; lanes without a limit render exactly as today
When n exceeds the limit, the count renders in a loud over state (red) with a hover title naming the limit
The n compares total epics in the lane (protocol semantics), not the filtered count, and the filtered 'X of N shown' behavior still works
Dragging a card into an over-limit lane is not blocked and writes normally
context: design/board.md (Column component, States); index.html render(); PROTOCOL §3 + wipBlocked() for the semantics being surfaced; idea-wip-gates-ui deep dive for the advise-only decision

name: Gate lock chips on epic cards
description: Epics-mode cards whose gate ≠ 'none' and isn't in open_gates wear a lock chip naming the gate — same visual language as rows mode's .egate badge. Open or absent gate → no chip. Existing move-guard semantics untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A card with a closed gate shows a chip naming the gate; gate 'none' or open (in open_gates) shows nothing
The chip's language matches the rows-mode .egate badge (one gate vocabulary across modes)
Opening the gate in config.json removes the chip on the live-reloaded page without a manual reload
Dragging a gated card behaves exactly as before — the chip advises, the protocol enforces
context: design/board.md (Card component, rows .egate for the shared language); index.html cardEl() + gateOpen(); idea-wip-gates-ui deep dive

name: context_docs chips in the epic modal, copy on click
description: The epic edit modal renders context_docs as read-only chips (label, with path/note as hover title); clicking a chip copies the path to the clipboard with a confirming toast, following the Ideas page's copy convention. No editing widget; section absent when the epic has no context_docs and on create.
acceptance_criteria: An epic with context_docs shows a read-only chip per doc in the edit modal (label visible; path and note in the hover title)
Clicking a chip copies the doc's path to the clipboard and a toast confirms
An epic without context_docs (and the create modal) shows no section at all
No input/edit affordance for context_docs exists anywhere in the modal — file/skill-only editing holds
context: design/board.md (Epic modal component); design/milestones.md + index.html ctxDocs() for the renderer being reused; AGENTS.md §2 no-widget stance; idea-context-docs-chips deep dive

name: Server: /api/pending — git-aware semantic board diff
description: server.js gains a git-read capability: /api/pending diffs the working data files against HEAD and returns card-level statements. Shared summarize function (old snapshot, new snapshot → statements) built for reuse by /api/history later.
acceptance_criteria: /api/pending returns JSON {clean, statements[], files[]} — clean:true with empty lists when the data dir matches HEAD
Statements are card-level: added / removed / moved (lane or status, old → new) / edited (changed field names) / reordered (one statement per resource, not N edits)
A card edited AND moved yields one combined statement, not two
Graceful degradation: no git repo or no commits yet → {clean:null, reason} without crashing; no shell injection (execFile, no string interpolation into a shell)
context: AGENTS.md §4 (commit = ratify), server.js existing route+watch style, roadmap/ideas.json idea-ratify-review Technical shape; the differ must treat array order as meaningful (queue order)

name: UI: pending badge + review panel
description: The header's saved dot gains a pending count; clicking opens a review slide-over listing the statements grouped by resource, live-updating via the SSE refresh path. Empty state: 'Everything ratified — board matches HEAD.' No write affordances.
acceptance_criteria: With uncommitted board changes, the header shows a pending count; clean tree shows the plain saved dot
Clicking opens the panel with card-level statements grouped by resource; a footer hint names the ratify convention ('save' in conversation / git commit)
The panel and badge update live while agents edit (SSE refresh path), and after saves from the page itself
Zero write affordances in the panel; clean tree shows the 'Everything ratified' empty state
context: design/system.md (header chrome — spec first per DESIGN.md), index.html wireLiveRefresh()/refresh() for the update hook, B3-1's endpoint

name: Ready-queue strip on the Board page
description: A strip beside Next up listing pickable stories ('[kind] B4-1 name' chips grouped under epic ids): ready + epic deps done + epic gate open + story unclaimed, ranked story priority → epic rank → file order. Click opens the story modal. Hidden when no stories exist; explains itself when stories exist but none are pickable.
acceptance_criteria: Every story satisfying PROTOCOL §3's story rule appears exactly once, grouped under its epic, ranked story-priority → epic rank → file order
Stories failing any condition (not ready, epic gated/blocked, claimed) do not appear; claimed ready stories don't appear
Click on a queue chip opens that story's modal
No stories on the board → strip absent; stories exist but none pickable → one-line reason (mirrors Next-up's empty language)
context: design/board.md (Next-up strip component — match its language), index.html nextUp()/renderNextUp()/gateOpen()/depsOf(), PROTOCOL §3 stories addendum

name: Server: /api/history — the data dir's git log
description: /api/history returns the data dir's commits (hash, date, message, files touched), newest first, capped; /api/history/<hash> returns that commit's card-level statements by running the B3-1 differ against its parent.
acceptance_criteria: /api/history returns [{hash, date, message, files}] for commits touching the data dir, newest first, capped (~50)
/api/history/<hash> returns the same statement format as /api/pending, diffing the commit against its parent (root commit: everything 'added')
Invalid/unknown hash → 404-style JSON error, no crash; execFile only, hash validated against /^[0-9a-f]{4,40}$/i
No-git and no-commit data dirs degrade gracefully like /api/pending
context: B3-1's summarize function and git plumbing in server.js; AGENTS.md §4 Board: commit convention

name: UI: #/history timeline page
description: A History nav tab and #/history page: one entry per ratification (relative date, message, files chips); expanding an entry lazily fetches its card-level changes. New design/history.md spec per the design contract.
acceptance_criteria: History tab in the nav renders the timeline newest-first with date, message, and files touched per entry
Expanding an entry fetches /api/history/<hash> once (cached thereafter) and shows card-level statements
Page is read-only; works when history is empty (fresh board) with an explanatory empty state
design/history.md exists (frontmatter, layout, components, interactions, states, data) and matches the built UI (spec_state: matches-ui)
context: design/DESIGN.md (spec file format), design/system.md (nav tabs, page chrome), B5-1 endpoints

name: FLIP-animate cards across live refreshes
description: Capture card rects before applyBoard, re-render as today, then FLIP moved cards with a lift effect; .flash pulse for edited-in-place; fade-in for new cards; reduced motion falls back to the instant snap. Board (epics + rows) and Ideas pages.
acceptance_criteria: An agent editing epics.json to move a card between lanes makes the card visibly lift, glide to the new lane, and set down on the open page (no reload)
A reorder glides the affected cards to their new positions; an edit-in-place pulses the flash ring without motion; a new card fades in
The user's own drags never trigger the animation (own-write echo skip), and prefers-reduced-motion falls back to the instant snap
Works on board epics mode, rows mode story cards, and ideas columns
context: design/system.md live refresh; index.html refresh()/render()/renderIdeas(); the approved FLIP plan

name: Exclude done-lane stories from the badge's ready count
description: cardEl()'s story badge: ready segment counts stories with ready: true whose column isn't the done lane; segment absent when that count is zero.
acceptance_criteria: A card whose ready stories are all in the done lane shows 'N stories' with no ready segment
A card with a ready story still pending shows that story in the ready count
Story count itself still includes done stories
context: design/board.md Story badge; index.html cardEl(); the ready-queue's finished-≠-stuck precedent

name: Palette overlay: fuzzy find + jump
description: '/' opens an overlay on the shared scrim: input + ranked results over an in-memory index of epics, stories, and ideas (subsequence fuzzy match). Arrow keys move the selection, Enter jumps (epic → board card flash; story → story modal; idea → deep-dive page), Escape closes. Shortcuts suppressed while typing in any field or while a modal is open.
acceptance_criteria: '/' anywhere (outside inputs/modals) opens the palette focused on its input; Escape closes it
Typing filters epics + stories + ideas by subsequence match, ranked sensibly; each result shows type, id, and title
Enter (or click) on an epic goes to the board and flashes the card; on a story opens its story modal; on an idea opens its deep-dive page
Arrow keys move the selection; '/' while typing in a form field does nothing
context: design/system.md (spec first); index.html goToEpic()/renderStoryModal()/navigate(); milestones arrow-key pattern; idea-command-palette deep dive

name: Quick capture: 'n' from anywhere
description: 'n' (outside inputs/modals) opens the new-idea modal from any page — capture lands in the Ideas inbox without navigating. Footer hints mention both shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: 'n' on any page opens the new-idea modal; creating navigates to the new idea's deep dive as usual
'n' while typing in a field or with a modal open does nothing
Footer hints name '/' and 'n'

name: Server: /api/since/<hash> — changes between a commit and HEAD
description: Reuse snapshotAt() + summarizeChanges() to diff an arbitrary earlier commit against HEAD; response carries the current HEAD hash so the client can advance its last-seen marker. Graceful when the hash is unknown (rewritten history) or git is absent.
acceptance_criteria: /api/since/<hash> returns {head, statements} diffing that commit → HEAD with the pending panel's statement format
Unknown/invalid hash → available:false JSON (no crash); hash validated like /api/history/<hash>
Same-hash-as-HEAD returns empty statements with head present
context: server.js git()/snapshotAt()/summarizeChanges(); B5-1's hash validation

name: Briefing banner: since-you-last-looked + stale claims
description: On load, compare the per-browser last-seen HEAD (localStorage, keyed by board title) with the current HEAD: if they differ, show a dismissible banner under the header — 'Since you last looked: N changes' — expandable to the card-level statements, plus stale claims (claimed >48h, not done) computed client-side. Dismiss stores the new HEAD. First visit stores silently.
acceptance_criteria: With a stored last-seen hash older than HEAD, the banner appears with the change count and expands to card-level statements
Dismiss stores the current HEAD and hides the banner; reload shows no banner until new commits land
First visit (no stored hash) stores silently with no banner
Claims older than 48h on non-done cards are listed as stale in the expanded view
context: design/system.md (spec first); index.html wirePending() pattern, localStorage modeKey() pattern; B9-1 endpoint

name: stop subcommand + kill hint in the port-busy error
description: board script gains 'stop [port]' (default 4300): report what's listening, kill it, confirm. server.js EADDRINUSE message names both escape hatches: ./board stop and the second-port option.
acceptance_criteria: ./board stop kills the listener on 4300 and reports the pid; ./board stop 4301 targets that port; nothing listening → friendly no-op
The port-busy error message tells the user to run ./board stop (or use PORT=)
Usage header and ./board list output mention stop

acceptance_criteria: A board with no briefing to show renders no banner at all (hidden attribute effective despite display:flex)

First-lane ready stories show '✓ ready' when pickable, '⛔ gated: <gate>' or '⏳ waiting on <dep>' when the epic is blocked, 'claimed' when claimed; not-ready shows a dim 'needs prep'
Labels are stable across re-renders (id-hash pooling, no randomness); epic modal story rows show the same chip read-only with the ready checkbox untouched
context: design/board.md; index.html storyCardEl()/storiesSection()/readyQueue() helpers; approved plan (state table)

name: archived_at + Current/Shipped toggle + archive action
description: Epic schema gains archived_at; epicShown() filters by view; (Current)(Shipped N) chips beside the view toggle; 'Ship & archive' button in the modal for epics whose stories are all done (Unarchive in shipped view); shipped view is read-only (no drag), next-up/ready strips hidden there; goToEpic follows the target into the right view; archived epics keep counting for milestones and deps.

name: AGENTS.md §0 orientation + contract drift fixes
description: A compact orientation section at the top of AGENTS.md (the first file the skill mandates) mapping the whole tool; PROTOCOL.md learns archived_at and states that shipped epics are out of the selection set; SKILL.md gains a current capability list and ./board stop.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md opens with an orientation section naming the five data files, the five UI surfaces, the inviolable rules, and where each detail lives — readable in under a minute

description: CAPABILITIES.md restructured for five surfaces (not 'three pages'), with story states and ./board stop added and the date bumped; README refreshed for humans; server.js serves AGENTS.md and PROTOCOL.md so an agent holding only the URL can read the contract it must follow.
acceptance_criteria: CAPABILITIES.md describes five surfaces accurately, mentions story-state vocabulary, ./board stop, and archived_at, with a current 'as of' date
README.md mentions the History page, ratify/briefing, palette, and shipped archive

The HTTP surface list in CAPABILITIES.md includes the new contract routes

name: Per-dependency chips + unblocked card treatment
description: Split the lumped dep badge into one chip per dependency, colored by state (✓ green when the dep is in the done lane, loud when not). Add .card.unblocked when a card has deps, all are satisfied, and nothing else blocks it (first lane, gate open, unclaimed): green left edge, faint wash, '▶ ready to start' marker. Rows mode's epic row header gets the same edge.
acceptance_criteria: A card with mixed deps shows each dep id as its own chip: satisfied ones green with ✓, unsatisfied ones in the warn color
A card whose deps are all satisfied and which is in the first lane, ungated and unclaimed, renders the unblocked treatment with a '▶ ready to start' marker
A card with satisfied deps that is gated, claimed, or already past the first lane does NOT get the treatment (it isn't startable)
Cards with no deps are visually unchanged; rows-mode row headers show the same edge for unblocked epics
context: design/board.md Dep badge/Card components; index.html cardEl(), depsOf(), gateOpen(), doneLane(), swimEl(); .bsec left-edge idiom for the visual language

name: Resolved-dependency chips on idea cards
description: Idea deps (informational sequencing, ids may name ideas or epics) get the same resolution chips — green ✓ once the named thing is done — but unresolved ones stay dim rather than loud, because no ordering rule is enforced on ideas.
acceptance_criteria: An idea whose dep names a done idea or a done epic shows that id green with ✓
Unresolved idea deps render dim (not the warn color) — informational deps must not look like violations
An idea dep naming an unknown id renders dim without breaking the line
context: design/ideas.md Dependencies line; index.html ideaCard() .idep, ideaById(), byId(), doneLane()

name: Unblocked treatment on idea cards
description: Ideas get the card-level signal too: when every dep an idea names has landed, the idea card takes the green edge, wash, and a '▶ clear to pursue' marker — the idea's sequencing precondition is met. Must beat the front-burner accent edge in the cascade without disturbing it.
acceptance_criteria: An active idea whose deps are all resolved shows the green edge, wash, and '▶ clear to pursue'
An idea with any unresolved dep, or with no deps at all, is visually unchanged
The treatment wins over the front-burner accent left edge, and back-burner cards can show it too
Archived (done/rejected) ideas never show it — there is nothing left to pursue
context: design/ideas.md; index.html ideaCard(), depChips(), .bsec:not(.back) .idea left-edge specificity

name: One meaning per colour: semantic state tokens
description: Named state tokens mapped onto the existing palette (aesthetic unchanged): gray back burner, blue front burner, purple ready-for-review, green ready-to-implement, amber blocked, red reserved for real problems. Applied as a 3px left border plus a matching status pill; heavy card tints removed, including B15's green 'clear to pursue' wash. Border carries workflow state only — never two dimensions at once.
acceptance_criteria: Every idea card's left border encodes exactly one thing — its workflow state — with gray/blue/purple/green per the legend, and a status pill in the same colour names it in words
Blocked shows as an amber pill and amber dep chips, never by recolouring the border (a card can be 'front burner' and 'blocked' at once without ambiguity)
Red appears nowhere except genuine problems (rejected ideas, over-WIP, refused moves) — unmet board deps become amber
No card carries a heavy background tint; any tint is barely-there, and the dark restrained aesthetic is unchanged
context: design/system.md tokens; design/ideas.md; index.html :root palette, .idea/.bsec CSS, .depid colours, B15's .unblocked wash

name: Five-second card: outcome, leverage, decision
description: Collapsed cards answer what/why/unlocks/how-hard/what's-stopping-us. Title, then a one-sentence outcome (first sentence of the description, clamped — no new field), then the pill row, then Unlocks (reverse dependencies, with an ↑ unlocks N leverage marker), Depends on, and a single decision-or-blocker line. Full prose moves to the deep dive.
acceptance_criteria: A card shows one sentence of outcome, not the full description; the deep dive still shows everything
Ideas that other ideas depend on show 'Unlocks: …' with a leverage count; ideas nothing depends on show no such line
The card ends with at most one decision-or-blocker line, and cards with neither stay compact
Card height for a typical arc idea is materially shorter than before while carrying more structured facts
context: index.html ideaCard(), descParts(); reverse-dep computation like unblockCount() for epics; design/ideas.md

name: why_now, decision, conviction — reasoning as data
description: Three idea fields: why_now (one line, expected on front-burner and review items), decision (the specific question a reviewer must answer), and conviction (speculative | promising | clear to pursue) as a dimension explicitly separate from workflow status. Schema in AGENTS.md §2, editable in the idea modal, rendered on the card and deep dive.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md §2 documents all three fields, including that conviction is orthogonal to status and that agents may propose but not finalise conviction
The idea modal edits all three; the deep-dive page renders them; absent fields render nothing anywhere
A 'ready for review' card shows its decision line prominently — the reviewer sees the question, not just the essay
Conviction renders as small text/pill distinct from the status pill, so 'Ready for review' + 'Clear to pursue' can coexist
context: AGENTS.md §2 idea schema; index.html openIdea()/saveIdea()/blankIdea()/renderIdeaDetail(); design/ideas.md + design/idea-detail.md

name: Maturity palette — one colour per card, and it's the stage
description: Ideas use a maturity scale: gray back burner, blue front burner, amber ready-for-review, green ready-to-implement. Everything else on an idea card goes neutral so nothing competes with the stage — the leverage marker and resolved-dep ticks stop rendering green, and the amber blocked pill is retired (amber now means 'decision required'). Red on ideas means rejected, nothing else.
acceptance_criteria: Idea edges and status pills follow gray → blue → amber → green by stage; purple is gone from the ideas page
No green appears on a back-burner or front-burner card — leverage and dependency marks render neutral
Red appears on an idea only when it is rejected
The execution board keeps its own state colours (gates/blocked amber, problems red) and is unaffected
context: design/system.md legend; design/ideas.md; index.html ideaCardState(), .lev, .depid, .spill

name: Progressive card detail — the same object gets more rigorous
description: Card content is a function of stage. Back burner: title, outcome, effort/impact. Front burner: adds why it matters, Opens, dependencies. Ready for review: leads with the decision. Ready to implement: outcome, constraints, dependencies-satisfied, acceptance boundary. 'Unlocks' is renamed 'Opens'; constraints and acceptance are new fields rendered only at the ready stage.
acceptance_criteria: A back-burner card shows title, outcome and effort/impact only — no why-now, Opens or dependency lines even when those fields hold values
A front-burner card adds why-now, Opens and dependencies; a review card leads with Decision needed
A ready-to-implement card shows outcome, constraints, dependencies-satisfied and acceptance boundary
The reverse-dependency line reads 'Opens:' everywhere, and the deep dive still shows every field regardless of stage
context: index.html ideaCard(), unlockedBy(), renderIdeaDetail(); AGENTS.md §2 for constraints/acceptance

name: Promote to Board — the graduation boundary
description: A ready-to-implement idea gets a 'Promote to Board' action that creates the execution epic seeded from the idea (title, description, theme, milestone, context docs, a notes line citing the idea), records promoted_to on the idea, marks it done with a dated log entry, and offers to jump to the new card. Discovery ends and delivery begins at one recorded moment.
acceptance_criteria: Promote appears only on ready-to-implement ideas, and only in the idea deep dive and modal — never as a drag
Promoting creates an epic in the first lane with the idea's content and a notes line naming the source idea id
The idea gains promoted_to (the epic id), moves to done with a dated log entry, and its card shows the link
Promoting twice is impossible — an already-promoted idea shows the link, not the button

name: Collapse Back Burner by default

name: Every prose region editable in place

Save writes and re-renders; Cancel restores; Escape from an editor does not lose the rest of the page

name: Every claim shows its age; old ones look suspect
description: Claimed epics and stories display who holds them and for how long, reusing sinceLabel(). Past the staleness threshold (48h, not in the done lane) the claim renders amber with an explanatory title — suspect, never auto-cleared, because a long-running job and an abandoned one are indistinguishable from outside.
acceptance_criteria: A claimed epic card and a claimed story both show the holder and how long ago it was claimed
A claim older than 48h on a card not in the done lane renders amber and says why on hover; a fresh claim renders normally
Claims on done cards are never marked stale — finished work is not waiting on anyone
No claim is ever cleared automatically

name: Release a claim in one action
description: A 'Release claim' action clears claimed_by/claimed_at from the epic modal, the story modal, and the work queue's in-flight rows. The work queue's empty state names how many of the blocking claims are stale, so a queue that looks empty explains what to release.
acceptance_criteria: A claimed epic and a claimed story can each be released from their modal in one action, and the card returns to its normal state
The work queue's in-flight rows offer release without opening a modal
When nothing is pickable because of claims, the queue's reason says how many of those claims are stale
Releasing writes claimed_by and claimed_at as null and persists once

name: Aggregate bar per milestone and per deliverable
description: A stacked progress bar under each milestone header showing its mapped epics bucketed by lane position (queued / in flight / done), with a done-fraction label; the same bar in miniature on each deliverable row. Pure client-side aggregation over epicsOfMilestone(); reuses the positional lane colours so the bar reads like the board it summarises.
acceptance_criteria: Each milestone with mapped epics shows one bar and an 'N of M epics done' label, and each deliverable row shows a mini-bar
Bar segments use the positional lane colours, so a milestone's bar matches the board's own vocabulary
Archived (shipped) epics still count toward both the numerator and the denominator
A milestone with no mapped epics shows no bar rather than an empty or zero one

name: Decode request bodies once, not per chunk
description: readBody accumulated with `data += chunk`, calling Buffer.prototype.toString() on each chunk in isolation. Collect the chunks and decode the whole body once.
acceptance_criteria: A body whose chunk boundary falls inside a multi-byte character round-trips intact
The size cap counts bytes rather than string length
Writing data that contains U+FFFD logs a warning naming the file, and still writes
Existing board data loads and saves unchanged
